title: Splash Patrol
summary: Inspect a tube water-slide built from function pieces: flag every gap and every kink before the test duck rides it.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Continuity at a point: left limit, right limit and value
A removable gap: limits agree but the value does not
Corners of |x − c| and of |cos x|, sin|x|
Jumps of the greatest integer function [x]
learningOutcome: The student can find every point where a piecewise, modulus or greatest-integer function is not continuous, and every point where it is continuous but not differentiable.

levels.title: Find the gaps
levels.adds: Baseline: f is continuous at c when the left limit, the right limit and f(c) agree; flag every joint where they do not (Ex 5.1 Q6 to Q16).
hints: At each joint, put x = c into the piece on the left and the piece on the right.
If the two give different numbers, the slide has a gap there.
Also check the value f(c) itself: a single wrong point is a gap too.

levels.title: Gaps and kinks
levels.adds: New: a joined slide can still have a kink: compare the slopes from the left and the right, as for |x − 1| at 1 (Ex 5.2 Q9; Ex 5.1 Q34).
hints: First check the values: a gap beats everything.
If the values agree, differentiate each piece and put in x = c.
Equal slopes: smooth. Different slopes: a kink.

levels.title: Steps and folds
levels.adds: New: [x] jumps at every integer, and |g(x)| can fold into a kink where g = 0 but not where g touches its peak (Ex 5.1 Q19, Q31 to Q33; Ex 5.2 Q10).
hints: [x] has a jump at each integer and is flat in between.
|g(x)| can have a kink only where g(x) = 0 and changes sign.
At a peak such as |cos x| at π, the slope is 0 on both sides: smooth.

levels.title: Chief inspector
levels.adds: Harder: sums and products of [x], |x| and pieces, such as [x] + |x − 1| and x[x]; some joints are traps (Ex 5.1 Q19, Q34; Misc Q20).
hints: Check each joint for a jump first, from any part of the sum.
x|x| is smooth at 0: its slope is 0 from both sides.
|x| + |x − 2| is flat between 0 and 2, so x = 1 is smooth.

misconceptions: A function that is continuous is also differentiable
If the left and right limits agree, the function is continuous whatever f(c) is
|g(x)| has a corner wherever g(x) has a turning point
